correctness.rationale: Model the regular module as F_q[u]/(u^n), with T=1+u. The base part of the p^b-power is multiplication by ((1+u)^i-1)^(p^b-1), using the geometric-sum identity in characteristic p. For i nonzero the factor in parentheses has valuation p^v_p(i) and unit leading coefficient, so the image is the corresponding principal ideal and kernel size is q to that valuation, capped at n. For admissible nonzero j, each of the p^b top preimages of j has valuation v_p(j)-b; for zero j, p^b-p^(b-1) preimages have valuation a-b and the remaining p^(b-1) base maps vanish. This derives all three fiber rules and their supports. The top-zero and top-p^b supports for b<a have ratio q^((p^b-1)(p^(a-b)-1)) taking the latter over the former, which is impossible for subgroup cosets. At b=a the support is the fixed line, attained nontrivially by a single-coordinate vector with i=1. At b>a all power maps vanish. Dividing the image formula by the group order and setting t=s-b gives truncations of the stated positive convergent series plus a vanishing zero-top term. A separate coordinate enumeration checked every target at depths 1 through a+1 for (p,q,a)=(2,2,3),(2,4,2),(3,9,1),(3,3,2),(5,5,1). It summed the shifted coordinate vectors directly and built the claimed ideals by repeated shift differences. Image sizes in the first case were 336,36,2,1; in the fourth were 4401,3,1.
residual_risks: Bounded replay is illustrative; the module proof covers every p,q,a,b. The asymptotic fixes p,q,b; no varying-depth limit is inferred.
